stages.title: Public sector pay: the drawbacks
stages.sub: How centrally set pay can cause problems for public services.

steps.q: Private firms raise wages for scarce skills quickly, but a public pay scale rises slowly by decision. Over time, who ends up paying more for skilled roles?
steps.hint: One side responds to the market, the other waits for a decision.

steps.q: With that pay gap, what do skilled public workers do, and how easy is it to fill their posts?
steps.right: They leave, and posts are hard to fill
steps.wrong: They stay, and posts are easy to fill
steps.hint: Skilled people can earn more elsewhere.

steps.q: Each year the government decides one pay rise for a whole group of public workers. Who decides the size of the rise?
steps.right: The government, for everyone in the group
steps.wrong: Each employer, for each worker separately
steps.hint: One decision covers the whole group.

steps.q: One national pay scale pays a nurse in London the same as a nurse in a cheap northern town. Where is it harder to recruit?
steps.right: London, where living costs are much higher
steps.wrong: The northern town, where living costs are lower
steps.hint: The same pay buys less where costs are higher.
